content.title: About
content.content: Biryani with vegetables is a fragrant Indian dish made from long‑grain basmati rice combined with a mix of vegetables, spices, and sometimes nuts. The dish balances the rich flavor of spices, the subtle sweetness of vegetables, and the characteristic aroma of saffron.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word biryani comes from the Persian “birinj”, meaning “fried rice”.
Traditionally it is cooked in a heavy clay pot called a “dhapti”, which traps steam and aroma.
The vegetable version is popular among vegetarians and those avoiding meat.
In some regions toasted onions and cashews are added for extra texture and flavor.
Biryani is often served with a yogurt‑based raita or mango chutney.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Basmati rice releases energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Carrots, peas, bell peppers and other veggies provide vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric, coriander and cumin contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and fennel stimulate bile production and aid digestive processes.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Biryani is typically prepared with a modest amount of oil, making it lighter than many fried dishes.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to turmeric, coriander or cumin.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The dish often includes soy sauce; those monitoring salt intake should reduce the amount.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Cooked rice left at room temperature for too long can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro, fried onions or lemon wedges. It pairs well with yogurt raita, chutney, or a simple salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the biryani to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat with a splash of water to restore moisture.
